description: 'Myth or fact?' statements with computed verdicts, generated by pipeline/myths.py.

items.answer: In 28 of 34 schemes apprentices earn a wage, and in 6 more an allowance.
items.source: Cedefop, European database on apprenticeship schemes (2026 fiches, coded answers)

items.answer: In 23 of 33 schemes the typical apprentice is 18 or older.
items.detail: In 8 schemes many apprentices are over 24 — apprenticeship is also a route for adults.
items.source: Cedefop, European database on apprenticeship schemes (2026 fiches, coded answers)

items.statement: Apprentices spend most of their time in a classroom.
items.answer: In 31 of 34 schemes apprentices spend about half their time or more at the company.
items.detail: In 13 of them it is two-thirds or more.
items.source: Cedefop, European database on apprenticeship schemes (2026 fiches, coded answers)

items.statement: An apprenticeship rules out going to university.
items.answer: 24 of 34 schemes lead to a qualification that gives direct access to higher education.
items.detail: In the other 10, the qualification does not by itself open the way to higher education.
items.source: Cedefop, European database on apprenticeship schemes (2026 fiches, coded answers)

items.answer: Employers pay apprentices in 33 of 34 schemes.
items.detail: The state contributes to apprentices' pay in 6 schemes, 5 of them alongside employers.
items.source: Cedefop, European database on apprenticeship schemes (2026 fiches, coded answers)

items.answer: 33 of 34 schemes require a written contract or agreement.
items.detail: 23 use a contract made specifically for apprentices.
items.source: Cedefop, European database on apprenticeship schemes (2026 fiches, coded answers)

items.statement: Apprenticeship is the main route in vocational education everywhere.
items.answer: In 23 of 31 schemes with data, apprentices are under 30% of vocational learners.
items.detail: Only in 3 are they more than 60%: apprenticeship is the main route in a few countries, a minority route in most.
items.source: Cedefop, European database on apprenticeship schemes (2026 fiches, coded answers)

items.statement: Companies must provide a mentor or trainer to take on apprentices.
items.answer: 34 of 34 schemes require training companies to have a mentor or in-company trainer.
items.detail: 34 require a suitable learning environment at the workplace.
items.source: Cedefop, European database on apprenticeship schemes (2026 fiches, coded answers)

items.statement: Employers can get financial support for training apprentices.
items.answer: In 32 of 34 schemes employers can get financial incentives for training apprentices.
items.detail: Subsidies are the most common (25 schemes), then tax deductions (17).
items.source: Cedefop, European database on apprenticeship schemes (2026 fiches, coded answers)

items.statement: Employers' organisations and trade unions help design apprenticeship qualifications.
items.answer: In 32 of 34 schemes the social partners help design the qualifications.
items.detail: They help design curricula in 28 schemes and take part in final assessments in 21.
items.source: Cedefop, European database on apprenticeship schemes (2026 fiches, coded answers)

items.statement: Most recent VET graduates in the EU have learned at work.
items.answer: In 2025, 66% of recent VET graduates in the EU had work-based learning during their studies.

items.statement: Vocational graduates find jobs less often than other young graduates.
items.answer: In 2025, 80.1% of recent vocational graduates in the EU were employed, against 66.8% of general-education graduates.
items.detail: Recent graduates are aged 20–34 and left education one to three years earlier.

items.statement: A master craftsperson qualification is at the same level everywhere in Europe.
items.answer: It sits anywhere from EQF 4 to EQF 6, depending on the country.
items.detail: EQF 6 in Austria and Germany; EQF 4 in Montenegro and Slovenia.
